newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Nine villagers die in Philippine army, rebel clash.
newsitem.headline: Nine villagers die in Philippine army, rebel clash.

text.p: Nine villagers were killed and 17 wounded when their houses were pounded by army mortars fired at fleeing Moslem rebels, military officials in this southern Philippine city said on Monday.

The victims, mainly women, were killed when the mortars hit five houses in the village of Carmen, about 110 km (68 miles) northeast of Cotabato city, Lieutenant Noel Detoyato, military spokesman for the southern Mindanao region, said.
Detoyato said the incident happened on Saturday when members of the rebel Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) fired shots at a group of soldiers.
The MILF men took refuge near the village and continued firing on the soldiers, Detoyato said, adding that the military was then forced to seek mortar cover.
The MILF's vice-chairman for political affairs Ghadzali Jaafar, speaking to Reuters by telephone, denied his group provoked the clash and blamed the army for killing civilians.
"Why should they fire at houses? If we withdraw to Malacanang (the presidential palace) will they fire at us?" he said.
Detoyato said a military team would investigate the incident.
The battle took place near a major irrigation project which has seen several clashes in the past.
The MILF has demanded its members be allowed to work at the dam site but the army has prevented them from doing so.
The frequent clashes have stalled the dam project, which was designed to irrigate vast areas of Mindanao.

The government recently signed a peace deal with the main Moslem group, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), but the MILF had stayed out of the talks saying Moslem interests were still suffering.
